claim: *Checked predicates over a structured model.* A structured model supplies the domain; invariants state properties over that domain; a checker evaluates them at a declared cadence. This is one executable-model pattern, not the definition of executability.

topology.description: Structured model supports domain predicates; checker evaluates invariants; dashed feedback refines predicates.

required_terms: Structured model Records · edges · states Job: free / leased / done
Invariants Stable IDs + declared domains leased ⇔ owner exists
Checker Model check · drift lint · validator
One executable-model pattern, not the definition of executability.
bw_encoding: Black outlines and arrows; white nodes; sparse 3–7% gray groups. Every non-solid relation is locally labeled; no distinction depends on color.
redesign: Native semantic redraw; colors replaced by labeled relations and line conventions.
alt: Three nodes run left to right: a structured model supports invariants, which are evaluated by a checker. A dashed feedback edge from the checker returns to the invariants, identifying recurring failure as a reason for a new or refined invariant. The lease example states that leased is equivalent to owner exists. This is one executable-model pattern, not the definition of executability. Black lines, white nodes and explicit labels carry the meaning without color.
